Requiring a dedicated differently named signature-line test is a prescriptive coverage requirement; preserving the existing accepted-name rules and stopping at the first invalid entry is the supported behavioral outcome.

The acceptance checks prescribe specific test surfaces, fixture categories, and command execution beyond the observable behavior required by the request and owner decisions.

The contract unnecessarily mandates adding a focused regression test specifically in `tests/test_blueprints.py` and colocating it with the dotted-name test; test form and location were not required by the public request or issue-time owner decision.

Acceptance requires a targeted test run with no warnings attributable to the change; warning-free execution was not established by the public request, audited repository behavior, or the owner's coverage decision.

Acceptance requires the specific internal routing mechanism—using the existing row-wise VLA comparison branch rather than generic `np.where`—although the supported contract only requires equivalent observable Q-VLA comparison behavior.

Requires explicit boolean-weight coverage for all-False weights, missing data, and Dataset operations; these are well-grounded compatibility expectations, but were not separately required by the public request or issue-time owner decisions.
